correctness.rationale: Reviewed RESULT.md lines 5–117 and the verification notes and supplied matrix checker by inspection. Each factor is Hilbert–Schmidt by the monomial generating sum and the subcritical Gaussian integral. The reproducing kernel of T is exp(tz²+conj(s) w̄²+r²zw̄); the second Gaussian integral gives Q=TT* with a=t+bs, b=r⁴/σ and c=σ^(-1/2). The bound 2|a|+b<1 gives p>2b and b<d≤1, including the possible cancellation a=0. For the spectral lemma the kernel is positive trace class also directly as cVV*, with Vf(z)=exp(az²)f(√b z). The larger root gives h=ad/(d−b²), |h|<1/2; applying the kernel to the stated entire generating family rescales its generating variable by b/d. The nonzero coefficients are eigenvectors of distinct eigenvalues, and equality of the diagonal trace and their geometric sum excludes any residual positive eigenvalue. Square roots and geometric summation give the claimed singular values and Schatten formulas. At fixed positive magnitudes, |a|² grows strictly with the phase cosine, d decreases strictly, and all singular values therefore grow strictly. Independently, a 48×48 monomial-basis computation at r=0.4, t=0.07 exp(0.47i), s=0.05 exp(−0.83i) agreed for the first four singular values (1.00754410097,0.16364855562,0.02658032510,0.00431726195), with max discrepancy about 2.2×10^−16; aligned and antialigned phases bracket those four values. The uploaded checker was not executed and finite agreement does not establish the spectrum.

evidence: Weedbrook et al. Eqs. (48)–(49) unitarily identify a Gaussian state with thermal factors indexed by its symplectic eigenvalues, and cite earlier Gaussian-state work. Olivares-style phase-space convention with vacuum variance 1/2: arXiv:2102.05748 Eqs. (126)–(128) gives geometric number-state weights with ratio N/(1+N).

Sang–Zhao includes this Gaussian kernel and its Theorem 5.2 gives all Schatten memberships and a geometric bound, not the exact sequence in the inspected passage. Howe's PDF was not accessible by the attempted route.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For one mode the thermal decomposition gives the whole normalized spectrum from one symplectic eigenvalue ν, with mean number N=ν−1/2 when [x,p]=i. The normalized positive Q lies in its domain because the Husimi density is Gaussian and 2|a|+b<1. The claim is not merely a sharpening of a Schatten bound in isolation.
searches: Howe, The oscillator semigroup, AMS proceedings

evidence: Write A=(1−b)²−4|a|²>0 and B=(1+b)²−4|a|²=A+4b. Rotate z so a is real and nonnegative. For x=√2 Re z, p=√2 Im z the Husimi covariance is diag(1/(1−b−2|a|),1/(1−b+2|a|)); the Weyl covariance subtracts I/2 (the vacuum Gaussian in the Husimi convolution). Thus ν=√(B/A)/2. The elementary Gaussian trace is c/√A. The known thermal weights (1−q)q^n with q=(ν−1/2)/(ν+1/2) now give λ_n(Q)=2c/(√B+√A) · ((√B−√A)/(√B+√A))^n.

Here d=(√B+√A)²/4 and q=b/d, so the formula is identically the frozen squared singular-value sequence. At fixed b,c, phase alignment increases |a|², decreasing A and B and shrinking √B+√A. Both the prefactor and q=4b/(√B+√A)² increase strictly, with positive prefactor and b. This proves the very same all-index ordering, including the extrema and the norm consequences, directly from the prior spectrum.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is a substitution into an applicable prior stronger theorem and monotonicity of two explicit positive factors. It covers the strict phase statement as well as the geometric spectrum. An elementary generating-function proof changes the proof presentation but does not preserve a distinct scientific finding on narrowing to phase order.

evidence: The normalized positive Gram operator Q/Tr Q has Gaussian Husimi density: its coherent-state diagonal is proportional to exp(2 Re(a z²)−(1−b)|z|²). This identifies a single-mode Gaussian state: the Fourier transform of the Husimi density equals the Weyl characteristic function times the vacuum Gaussian.
Dong–Zhu's kernel coincides up to scalar r with this T when s=−t, using S=r^(−2), τ=2t/r². That identification alone only covers the equal-magnitude opposite-phase slice.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A Bargmann–Fock Gram kernel need not be written in the restricted canonical Fock form to apply the general Gaussian state result. Once normalized, its Gaussian state spectrum is exactly the squared singular spectrum of T divided by its trace. The coherent-state diagonal identification is valid for every a,b from the frozen hypotheses, not just a phase slice.

originality.rationale: The full spectrum and its strict ordering are covered by the known thermal normal form for a Gaussian density operator plus a direct one-mode covariance substitution. This is stronger coverage than a geometric upper bound or the restricted canonical Fock SVD; it does not require anyone to have previously used the submitted notation or stated its relative-phase comparison verbatim. The explicit implication below covers all independent phases and all indices. No distinct surviving scientific claim was established for repair.
residual_risks: Exact first publication of a formula in the submitted Bargmann notation was not determined.
Howe's exact treatment could provide a more direct ancestor, but failure rests on the inspected normal form and its explicit implication rather than inaccessible material.
